body:
First complete native campaign over the four governed roots (revision c8e3917, Python 3.11, mutmut 3.8.0, pytest 9.1.1): 29,811 mutants, 19,248 killed, 3,010 survived, 7,501 without a covering test, 6 timeouts, 46 segmentation faults. L4 aggregate 65.5% (required 98%); 27 modules pass their own threshold, 32 fail, 30 are incomplete. Gate verdict: FAIL; no certification is claimed.

The run exposed and fixed five defects in the migration (fnmatch scope semantics, pytest/mutmut pin, sandbox test selection, flat research imports, clean-checkout directory). Details, per-module scores and the remaining work are in `docs/thesis-remediation/RISK_MUTATION_MIGRATION.md` and `evidence/risk-native-campaign-2026-11-07.json` on PR #117.

Open: tests for the 7,501 uncovered mutants and 3,010 survivors, a decision for two modules that receive no native mutants, the segmentation faults, a cache/sharding plan for the hosted deep job, and independent review.

Progress on the open decisions (branch `feat/risk-tiered-mutation-policy`, PR #117; baseline campaign figures unchanged, no certification claimed):

- Zero-mutant modules: mutmut does generate mutants for `__main__.py` (39) and `logging_setup.py` (10); none were produced because no test covered them. With new tests: 35/36 and 10/10 killed in focused native runs. No `NOT_APPLICABLE` class introduced.
- Reviewed equivalence: versioned record file, strict binding (identity, source and catalog hashes, risk, policy version, independent reviewer), raw and adjusted scores reported separately, regression tests for acceptance, rejection, staleness and duplicates. No equivalent is accepted yet; independent review is pending.
- Sharding: deterministic plan, per-shard evidence manifests, fail-closed aggregation and a manual workflow with run-keyed caches that are saved even when scores fail. One real shard (15 modules, 5,618 mutants) was executed locally end to end. The workflow cannot be dispatched until it exists on the default branch, and the release gate does not consume the aggregate yet.
- Focused survivor work: `pool_preprocessing` 96.0%, `pool_train_only` 97.9%, `mutation_shards` 97.5% (remaining survivors reviewed, mostly case-insensitive path or default-argument variants).

Still open: 7,501 uncovered mutants, about 3,000 survivors, 46 segmentation faults and 6 timeouts (not yet investigated), release-gate integration of the aggregate, independent review.

Hosted validation and release integration (PR #117):

- Pre-merge trigger added: `pull_request` limited to same-repository PRs with the label `run:mutation-shards`, read-only token, concurrency-cancelled, every job checked out at the PR head SHA. The first hosted sharded campaign (run 42393637254, commit 20342c2) completed all six shards and the aggregate. Verdict FAIL: 31,137 mutants, 19,983 killed, 3,891 survived, 7,252 without tests, 11 timeouts, 0 segmentation faults (the 46 local faults were macOS-specific). L4 65.1%, L3 49.2%, L2 10/10. Shard times 19.5 to 49.3 min, so the count-based balance needs measured durations.
- Sharded evidence now uses the same `deep` contract as a monolithic campaign (re-derived from current plan, manifests, policy, source, tests, configuration and tools; tampered, stale, foreign, duplicated, missing or forged evidence is rejected). It is capped at INCOMPLETE until shards carry an execution-binding proof, so no certification path is weaker. Historical global evidence stays rejected.
- Also fixed: the release assessment no longer applies the legacy file-scope check to format-2 evidence (it would have rejected any passing campaign); mypy gate (pinned 2.4.0) passes after fixing five errors in the new module; REAL profile passes locally on the three datasets.
- Not yet done: cache restore and second-run reuse on hosted runners, execution-binding for shards, tests for the 7,252 uncovered and 3,891 surviving mutants, independent review.

Execution proofs and cache validation (PR #117):

- CI for 9807ce8: the earlier typing failure (20342c2) is fixed; runs were still in progress when checked.
- Sharded campaigns now require a controller execution proof per shard (native command equal to the shard's own patterns, exit status, per-module source and verdict-metadata digests, shared test and dependency digests, runtime). A campaign with every shard bound can pass; unbound stays INCOMPLETE; bound but below threshold fails. 18 regression tests cover missing, forged, stale, foreign, contradictory and mixed proofs.
- A real controller-bound shard ran locally (557 mutants, 495 killed, exit 0) and its manifest verified.
- Cache check on that shard: unchanged rerun kept 557/557 (1 min vs about 10); one edited test reset 180 covered mutants; one edited function reset 40; an edited verdict in a metadata file was not trusted.
- Focused measurements: `verification/claims.py` 5 to 599 of 714 (sandbox selection fix), `release.py` 557 to 680 of 827, `injection` 96.1%, `normalise` 90.7%, `uci_loader` 84.4%. The pool pipelines' `main`/`run_job` entry points (about 1,000 mutants) have no tests; that is next.
- Not changed: no equivalence accepted, thresholds fixed, no hosted rerun (label removed).

Progress (PR #117, head 2c5d0d1; focused local measurements unless stated, none bound to a campaign):

- Pool pipelines: new tests for job selection, loading, per-problem execution and both commands (`research/tests/test_pipeline_entry_points.py`, `test_pool_contracts.py`, with independent threshold oracles). `research/labelled_benchmark.py` 112/475 to 449/475 (94.5%), `research/pool_full.py` 223/515 to 491/515 (95.3%). The remaining survivors are mainly case-insensitive path variants (macOS) and `flush`/help arguments.
- Label and cleaning boundaries (`test_label_and_cleaning_contracts.py`): `research/uci_loader.py` 157/186 to 179/186 (96.2%), `research/normalise.py` 175/193 to 185/193 (95.9%).
- Hosted execution proof: a non-certifying diagnostic shard (label `run:mutation-shard-diagnostic`, shard 31 of 45) ran on a hosted runner with the controller: correct SHA, shard patterns in the native command, exit 0, manifest with proof summary, artifacts transported. 557 mutants, 367 killed. A second run restored the cache and the controller kept 557/557 verdicts (no resets).
- Open: the same shard kills 128 more mutants locally (macOS) than hosted (Linux), all in `research/lstm_detector.py`; cause unknown. Hosted invalidation after a test/source change was shown locally only.
- Unchanged: thresholds fixed, no equivalence accepted, classification unchanged pending independent review, shard aggregation still requires every shard to be bound, no full hosted campaign rerun.

Cross-platform LSTM discrepancy resolved (PR #117, fce7ca7):

- By stable identity, 429 of 557 shard-31 mutants agree between the local macOS and hosted Linux runs; 128 differ, all `killed` locally and `survived` on Linux, all in `research/lstm_detector.py`. None killed only on Linux, none untested, no differing error or timeout outcomes. Source, mapped tests, mutmut, pytest, python and torch (2.15.0) are identical, so versions do not explain it.
- Direct execution of the mapped tests with the mutant active (mutmut order, forked child after warm-up, controller thread settings) passed for a random sample of 16 of the 128 and for three inspected in detail, as it does unmutated. The local kills come from a failure of the forked macOS worker that direct runs do not reproduce (traceback not captured), like the 46 macOS-only segmentation faults. The hosted Linux verdict is the supported one; the detector still lacks tests for these mutations (for example the zero-variance `scale_` guard).
- Policy: release policy v2 now requires `deep_platform: "Linux"` for risk-tiered campaigns; macOS runs are diagnostics only. Evidence already binds platform and package versions and aggregation rejects mixed contexts. No dependency lock needed (identical torch).
- CI for dca8eae is green (FAST, TOOLS, faults). Superseded `verify-release` runs were cancelled.

Fork-server diagnostic (run 42433394723, d296f2f; hosted Linux, non-certifying, controller-bound, native exit 0): `research/lstm_detector.py` 377 mutants, 366 killed, 11 survived, 0 timeouts. `process_isolation = "forkserver"` resolved all 46 timeouts of run 42415522768 (PyTorch is documented as not fork-safe under the default isolation); the 60x timeout factor alone had not. Outcomes agree with direct mutant-by-mutant execution for 376 of 377 identities; the one difference (`spread > 0` to `> 1`) was platform-arithmetic dependent and is now killed by a test for a spread below one, as is the initial-stale-counter mutant. Expected 368/377 (97.6%) from direct evaluation (not a hosted number), below L4 (370 needed). The nine remaining survivors are listed as equivalence candidates with arguments in `docs/thesis-remediation/EQUIVALENCE_CANDIDATES_LSTM_2026-11-08.md`; none accepted, no independent reviewer yet.

Also pushed: source-clustered re-analysis with an independent numerical check (intervals agree within 0.001; One-Class SVM 84 problems, 68 sources), partition recovery, shard execution proofs. Still open: reviewer for equivalences, the other L4 modules, hosted invalidation and interrupted-shard checks.

Governance and equivalence (PR #117, 23f3757):

- The reviewer-must-differ-from-author rule is replaced by a declared sole-author owner-review model (`review_mode: sole_author_owner_review`, owner `theobigand` in the risk policy). Equivalence documents are version 2: verdicts proposed/accepted/rejected/inconclusive, recorded approver and date, dependency versions relied on, and non-authorizing assessments. Only an `accepted` record by the declared owner, bound to source digest, module-catalog digest, risk level, policy version and the campaign runtime's dependency versions (torch added to the recorded runtime), and naming a surviving mutant, leaves the adjusted denominator; raw outcomes and scores are always kept. Stated limits: not independent peer review; approver is recorded text, not a signature. 40 regression tests cover valid owner approval, wrong owner, wrong mode/version, stale source or catalog, dependency drift, non-surviving mutants, duplicates, and the raw/adjusted arithmetic; TOOLS coverage remains 100%.
- Nine LSTM candidates are proposed (none decided) in `docs/thesis-remediation/equivalence/lstm_proposals_2026-11-11.json` with exact diffs, scope of each argument and assistant/GPT-6 assessments (four universal ACCEPT proposals, five INCONCLUSIVE environment-bound ones). The consolidated owner decision packet is `EQUIVALENCE_REVIEW_PACKET_LSTM_2026-11-08.md`. Accepting the four universal ones would give adjusted 368/373 (98.7%) if the expected 368 kills are confirmed hosted; that confirmation is still pending.
- Pending owner decisions: the nine verdicts above. No approval is assumed.

Hosted diagnostic run 42985826795 (shard 31, 3dbf6f5, Linux, torch 2.15.0+cpu) finished: research/lstm_detector.py 368 killed, 9 survived, 0 timeout, 0 incomplete of 377. The 9 survivors are exactly the 9 owner-reviewed mutants. Raw 368/377 = 97.61% (below L4 98%); adjusted after the 4 owner-accepted equivalences 368/373 = 98.66% (meets 98%, exact integers). The 5 inconclusive records stay eligible. pool_check.py in the same shard: 118/180 killed (65.6%). Diagnostic only: one shard, no release gate, no certification; sole-author owner review, not peer review. Evidence and details: docs/thesis-remediation/MUTATION_DIAGNOSTIC_RUN_42985826795.md. Also pushed: fix so non-accepted equivalence records no longer require a surviving mutant (16a83d4). Issue stays open.

No change to the mutation status. The LSTM diagnostic (368/377 raw 97.61%, 368/373 adjusted 98.66%, four sole-author owner-accepted equivalences, five inconclusive still eligible) is now also stated in the manuscript and slide 40 as a one-module diagnostic that certifies nothing; slide 1 corrected (historical core mutation is 97.61%, 4,980 of 5,102, not 97.45%). pool_check.py (118/180, 65.6%) still needs targeted tests. verify-release remains label/dispatch only.

Focused local mutation diagnostics, 2026-11-11 (raw scores, no equivalence accepted, thresholds unchanged): pool_check 118/180 to 178/180, alert_budget 766/780, alert_budget_summary 123/123, matched_alert 317/322, prevalence_shift 363/369, score_shift 795/806, source_clustered 333/337; normalise 188/197 (95.4%) and paired_bootstrap 94/100 remain below L4. Finding: MIN_CLASS_COUNT = 3 in research/normalise.py is below the 6 anomalies a 70/15/15 stratified split needs (3 to 5 raise a raw ValueError that build_pool does not catch); left unchanged because archived manifests hash the file, owner decision needed. No full campaign was run, the release gate stays fail-closed. Details: docs/thesis-remediation/MUTATION_FOCUSED_DIAGNOSTICS_2026-11-11.md

Progress on `feat/risk-tiered-mutation-policy` (2026-11-12, HEAD 3b5e59d). Raw focused scores only; they are not a campaign and not certification, and no checkbox above changes.

Focused results (killed/total): paired_bootstrap 100/100, typed_masking 132/132, build_pool 169/172, labelled_benchmark 471/475, pool_typed 517/525 (those four at or above 98 raw), typed_run 342/351 (97.4%), normalise 191/197 (96.95%), quality/base 30/31, load 13/14, temporal_pilot 542/586 (92.5%).

Inventory: 91 L4 modules in the policy; 82 in the 2026-11-07 campaign (56 below 98); 9 absent from it (six of the nine modules I measured earlier are among them). Generated table: `docs/thesis-remediation/MUTATION_L4_INVENTORY.md`.

Equivalence candidates (kept eligible, no approval requested or implied): normalise x6, build_pool x3, load x1, quality/base x1, and the sort=None / astype(None) / aware-datetime / argparse-default kinds in the typed and temporal modules. Details and the owner decision needed: `MUTATION_FOCUSED_DIAGNOSTICS_2026-11-11.md`.

Scientific side effect: MIN_CLASS_COUNT is now 6 (fewer than six of a class made the 70/15/15 split fail with a bare ValueError); no archived labelled problem has fewer than six, no manifest was restamped.

Blockers: 56 campaign modules still below 98, the 9 absent modules, owner decisions on equivalences, full release verification not run. Release gate stays fail-closed.

Status at `1d518af` (CI green on this exact commit; PR #117 stays a draft; no certification claim).

- `to_timestamps` now refuses infinite elapsed times with a clear error. The archived Credit Card `Time` column is finite (0 to 172,792 s), so the archived temporal pilot is unaffected and its record keeps the script of its own revision. No archived evidence was restamped.
- Focused raw mutation scores (same method, below the 98 % L4 bar): `temporal_pilot` 571/589 (96.94 %, 1 timeout), `typed_run` 343/351 (97.72 %). Earlier in this stretch: `typed_masking` 132/132, `pool_typed` 517/525, `labelled_benchmark` 471/475.
- Remaining survivors in both modules are candidate-inert (`utc=` on already aware columns, `astype(None)` on numeric data, `sort=None`, argparse defaults equal to fallbacks). None is approved; reaching 98 % would need 6 (`temporal_pilot`) and 1 (`typed_run`) accepted, which requires the owner.
- `make mutation-focus MODULE=<module>` drops only the derived test-selection map before a focused run, which fixes the stale "no tests" case.
- Not done: full campaign, replays, the synthetic PCA discrepancy (0.4818 regenerated vs 0.56 archived; pandas and Faker versions excluded), T062, T063, T089, T172 (all still open).

Owner equivalence review packet, pushed at `bbfd7dc` (CI green on this exact commit; PR #117 stays a draft; release gate fail-closed; no certification claim).

**No owner approval was created.** All 43 candidates are stored as `verdict: proposed`, empty approver and decision date, outside `verification/mutation_equivalence.json`. The accepted denominator is unchanged.

- Packet: `docs/thesis-remediation/OWNER_EQUIVALENCE_REVIEW_2026-11-12.md`; proposals: `docs/thesis-remediation/equivalence/owner_review_candidates_2026-11-12.json`; survivors with diffs and digests: `docs/thesis-remediation/evidence/mutation-survivors-2026-11-12.json`.
- Technical assessment (not a verdict): 26 strong equivalence evidence, 17 additional verification required, 0 meaningful difference, 0 insufficient evidence, across 13 modules. Precedent: the owner left `astype(None)` and `replace=None` inconclusive on 2026-11-11; several candidates have that shape.
- Before building it I added behavioral tests that reduced the 49 survivors in the first eight modules to 26 (window boundary at the change time, naive timestamps, time-block integer type, configured split ratios, the deprecated pandas `unit="S"` alias, default method sets, flushed progress, wrong-length Holm). A pathological timeout (`temporal_pilot` bootstrap, `index = None`) is now killed. One alert-budget mutant ended once with exit code 255 (incomplete) and was killed on rerun.
- Arithmetic corrected: for the earlier 571/589 temporal measurement, six exclusions give 97.94 % (below 98), seven give 98.11 %; `typed_run` 343/351 with one exclusion is exactly 98.00 %. Both are superseded by the new focused scores below.
- Raw focused scores (development measurements, not a campaign): temporal_pilot 580/589, typed_run 349/351, typed_masking 132/132, pool_typed 521/525, labelled_benchmark 475/475, matched_alert 320/322, prevalence_shift 366/369, source_clustered 336/337, alert_budget 777/780, score_shift 800/806, pool_check 178/180, paired_bootstrap 100/100. Still below 98: normalise 191/197 (96.95 %), load 13/14, quality/base 30/31, all with candidates only.
- Still open: 56 campaign L4 modules below 98 and 9 absent from the campaign, the synthetic PCA discrepancy, T062, T063, T089, T172. No manuscript or slide change was needed.

Local L4 mutation measurement, 2026-11-13, HEAD `2c1ab3b` (CI success; `verify-release` and `mutation-shards` skipped as designed, no DEEP run). Development measurement with native mutmut on macOS, not the controller campaign, not a certification.

- 100 classified units, 34,778 mutants, 31,383 killed (90.24 %). Raw per-unit result: 44 pass, 1 pass after the four accepted LSTM equivalents, 48 fail, 4 incomplete (a timeout or a mutant no test reaches), 3 have no mutant (no function).
- By level: L4 (79 units) 39 pass / 36 fail / 4 incomplete; L3 (18) 5 / 12 / 1; L2 (3) 1 pass, 2 without mutant.
- The 12-file L4 to L3 reclassification the owner accepted is applied (`verification/mutation_risk_policy.json`); thresholds are unchanged.
- About 170 tests were added across the research, quality and verification modules; they took many modules from 25 to 60 percent to above 90 (e.g. `lstm_pilot` 130 to 460 of 506, `deep_typed` 223 to 415 of 442, `mutation_policy` 771 to 860 of 869).
- Timeouts count as not killed: `temporal_decision._block_ci` 25, `mutation_cache.prepare_execution` 128, `pool_contract.sha256_file` 6 and 14.
- Exact per-unit table and reproduction: `docs/thesis-remediation/L4_CAMPAIGN_REPORT_2026-11-13.md`; data: `docs/thesis-remediation/evidence/l4-campaign-2026-11-13/final-measurement.json`.
- No owner approval was created or inferred; the 43 candidates of the review packet stay proposed. PR #117 stays a draft.

Correction to the previous summary, after an independent review of the measurement (HEAD `e2576a0`).

- The one `PASS_ADJUSTED` unit I reported (`research/lstm_detector.py`) is not reproduced here. The four accepted LSTM equivalences pin `torch 2.15.0+cpu`; the local mutation venv has `torch 2.15.0`, so `mutation_policy.accepted_equivalents` refuses them. Without them the unit is 368/377 raw (97.61 %), a fail. Corrected totals: 44 pass raw, 49 fail, 4 incomplete (a timeout or a mutant no test reaches), 3 without mutants.
- The L4 to L3 move turns exactly one unit from fail to pass: `research/pool_extension_paper.py` (622/652, 95.40 %).
- The report now says which units are a few kills short and which survivors are in the owner packet, and the equivalence-class wording no longer treats `astype(None)` or `replace=None` as settled (the owner left them inconclusive).
- Report: `docs/thesis-remediation/L4_CAMPAIGN_REPORT_2026-11-13.md`.

Behavioral test remediation, local measurement (not a certification), HEAD `eb5f92a`.

- Totals: 60 pass (raw), 35 fail, 2 incomplete, 3 without mutants (was 44 / 49 / 4 / 3 at `e2576a0`); 33,302 of 34,781 mutants killed (was 31,383 of 34,778). Thresholds, risk levels, the 12 accepted L4 to L3 moves and `verification/mutation_equivalence.json` are unchanged; no owner approval was created; the only production change is the `research/time_scan.py` fix below.
- Units that now meet their threshold by the exact integer rule: evidence_schema, reproduce, release, claims, mutation_catalog, mutation_run, mutation_shards, mutation_campaign, dataset_registry, deep_typed, full_registry, full_registry_summary, labelled_summary, typed_summary, time_scan, cost_study. `mutation_cache` (1088/1110) and `pool_contract` (184/187) reach the raw score but carry non-terminating mutants (`sha256_file` 6 and 14, `prepare_execution` 128); they stay incomplete, not passing.
- Measurement platform: pytest temp folders on macOS are case-insensitive, so mutants that only change the case of a path survived locally. The units listed in the report's table were re-run on a case-sensitive volume; their verdict files are adopted with `measured_on` recorded, so the per-unit change mixes new tests and that effect.
- Still failing: 35 units, mostly (a) survivors that look equivalent (`astype(None)`, `sort=None`, a split limit, an attribute initialised to an empty string...), grouped in a second proposed-not-approved packet `OWNER_EQUIVALENCE_REVIEW_PACKET_2_2026-11-14.md` with counterexample searches (mutants that already have an owner verdict are listed apart, not re-proposed), and (b) large untested files (real_preflight, scaling, typed_figures, lock_environment, multi_schema, lstm_pilot, protection, refresh_profile, archive_evidence, paper_appendix, paper_tables, uci_pool).
- Found on the way: `research/time_scan.py` skipped date-text columns under pandas 3 (text is `str`, not `object`); fixed with regression tests, no change on the 116 local pool tables (`evidence/time_scan_impact.py`). The synthetic PCA discrepancy (0.4818 against the archived 0.56) is explained by a full-rank PCA whose scores are rounding noise; the value follows the numerical back end (0.5645 in the conda environment); archived values are untouched and the paper wording is an owner decision (`PCA_REPRODUCIBILITY_2026-11-12.md`).
- An independent review returned CHANGES_REQUIRED; the packet wording, class patterns, a test that caused a spurious timeout, test coupling and the provenance of the adopted verdicts were fixed in this head.
- Report: `docs/thesis-remediation/L4_CAMPAIGN_REPORT_2026-11-13.md`. PR #117 stays a draft; nothing is merged and no release gate is opened.

L4 remediation pass, HEAD 9ca176f (draft PR #117 unchanged, not merged, no gate opened, no certification).

Local mixed-platform measurement (case-sensitive volume for the units re-run, macOS case-insensitive APFS otherwise): 75 PASS_RAW, 22 FAIL, 3 NO_MUTANTS, 0 INCOMPLETE; 34,229 of 34,781 mutants killed (was 60 / 35 / 2 / 3 and 33,302). Full suite 4,013 passed, 23 deselected; ruff clean.

- New behavioral tests for real_preflight, scaling, typed_figures, lock_environment, multi_schema, protection, lstm_pilot, refresh_profile, archive_evidence, paper_appendix, pool_etl, uci_pool, paper_tables and the pool contract.
- The three non-terminating mutants (pool_contract.sha256_file 6 and 14, mutation_cache.prepare_execution 128) are killed by read-count budgets, not by a clock.
- Remaining 22 failing units are mostly equivalence candidates (unset state, truthy flags, default arguments, case-insensitive names, division by -1); they are listed in OWNER_EQUIVALENCE_REVIEW_PACKET_2 (PROPOSED, approves nothing). No threshold, level, policy or equivalence file changed.
- Not done: Linux/PyTorch check of lstm_detector (no Linux environment here; the official records pin torch 2.15.0+cpu and are refused locally), official DEEP/release verification.
- An independent review returned CHANGES_REQUIRED on report wording, environment labels and packet staleness; those findings are fixed in this push. The reviewer had no Git access.

Details: docs/thesis-remediation/L4_CAMPAIGN_REPORT_2026-11-13.md.

Reconciliation checkpoint (historical measurement at `9ca176f`; no certification): the archived ledger contains 34,781 unique mutant IDs, including 34,229 kills and 552 survivors. The 22 failing units account for 212 survivors: 33 second-packet proposals, eight first-packet proposals, four previously accepted LSTM records, five previously inconclusive LSTM records and 162 unclassified. Packet identities match the archived verdicts. CI test, faults and slides passed; mutation and release jobs were skipped.

A new public-contract GX test exposes two previously surviving mutants: a data frame whose index has the same name as a column must retain its index and yield the correct anomaly flags. Both mutants fail this test; the original and 41 focused detector tests pass. This is not yet a refreshed mutation-unit measurement. The source measurement mixes macOS filesystem environments and reused verdicts, and remains historical.

The independent review of the partial checkpoint returned CHANGES_REQUIRED for two wording errors; those statements were corrected locally, with no subsequent independent approval. The four LSTM exclusions remain rejected locally, and the synthetic PCA numerical discrepancy remains unresolved. Full campaign remeasurement, individual triage, Linux validator verification, independent review and official DEEP/release checks remain open. PR #117 remains a draft.

Full suite in the mutation venv: 4,013 passed, 23 deselected, one failure. The real Cardio archive reproduction was statistical where the test requires numerical equality on the same platform. The same test passed in the canonical conda environment; the cause has not been isolated. This is a separate reproducibility concern, not a full-suite pass.

Further Cardio investigation: replacing only the mutation interpreter's pandas package with the canonical pandas build restored numerical equality. The two builds parsed 17,081 raw CSV values differently (maximum absolute difference 1.78e-15); supplying the canonical loaded numeric values to the mutation environment also restored numerical equality. This identifies the observed input-parsing cause without changing the test or archive. A separate multi-schema mutant was shown to change per-type precision from 0.5 to 1.0; the remaining unclassified identities are recorded as inconclusive pending investigation. The focused native GX unit remeasurement completed: 89/98 killed, nine survived, eight further kills needed at L4. It used case-insensitive macOS and is not combined with the historical case-sensitive result. A native single-mutant rerun also killed the multi-schema precision mutant; no full multi-schema unit rerun has been completed.

Checkpoint commit `a9c2f1d5c0306d1b643c03d31a2c5938a76b3692` is pushed to draft PR #117. The canonical full suite on its test tree passed: 4,016 passed, 23 deselected; lint and formatting passed. Two additional pool-chronology tie-order mutants were killed by a meaningful regression and a native focused run. Preliminary triage now contains five focused kills and 157 inconclusive entries; the historical mixed-origin 100-unit totals have not been rewritten.

The final authorized independent review passed the earlier bounded checkpoint, not campaign certification, and did not cover the later pool regression. The current 45-shard plan places LSTM in shard 33, but the diagnostic workflow hardcodes shard 31; it cannot validate LSTM at this head. No current-head compatible Linux validator run, fresh 100-unit campaign, official DEEP or release verification has been completed. Ordinary CI for this checkpoint subsequently passed. The mutation-environment full suite still fails the Cardio numerical test; the parsing cause is documented without changing its assertion. No policy, risk, threshold or owner decision was changed.

Further checkpoint commit `0896dfc7b20516f80597fa302a019cace5731133` adds an inclusive H4 threshold regression and an injection index-collision regression. Three targeted mutants were killed in a native focused run; the 162-record preliminary triage now has eight focused kills and 154 inconclusive cases. The complete canonical suite on this test tree passed: 4,018 passed, 23 deselected; lint, formatting, focused provenance and policy-invariance checks passed. The bounded independent PASS predated these later regressions; no final campaign review or certification is claimed. Exact-head ordinary CI passed (`test`, `faults`, and `slides`, run 43637270417); mutation-shard and release jobs were skipped. Historical campaign totals remain 34,229/34,781 and must not be combined with the later focused runs.

Diagnostic routing checkpoint: commit `ced29750ab28515d00cb41a2f901a6bc2518e838` selects the requested module from the validated current shard plan. The LSTM diagnostic has started in hosted Linux run 43641178258 and selected shard 33; its results and current-head validator outcome are not yet available. The change has not received independent review. The historical mixed-environment ledger is unchanged; 154 of the 162 formerly unclassified records remain inconclusive. PR #117 remains draft, and the release gate remains closed. The canonical conda suite is in progress. `environment.yml` permits a pandas range and does not pin the build responsible for the recorded Cardio parsing behavior. No policy, equivalence decision or scientific archive was changed.

Correction on reproducibility: the repository also provides `verification/environment/conda-darwin-arm64.explicit.txt`. Its pandas 3.0.6 build `np2py311h0e7d951_0` and package SHA-256 `c7dff4fedcb00308b4fee9659f1085c45b9820113bd1f551971de8943180efb2` match the canonical environment's conda metadata. The repository's reproduction workflow can rebuild this platform-specific environment; this is stronger than the unpinned `environment.yml` alone. It does not guarantee the same parsed input on other platforms.

Resume details: the routing change alone does not execute `verification.mutation_policy.accepted_equivalents` on the runner. The hosted artifact must be validated in a matching Linux/PyTorch environment, or a separately tested diagnostic validator step must be added and rerun at the resulting HEAD. The diagnostic is not a complete 100-unit campaign. The full canonical suite log is `/tmp/etl-diagnostic-canonical-suite.log`; it was still running when this note was written. The retained untracked `experiments/results/cardio-env-audit/` is prior evidence and must be preserved.

- 101 equivalence exclusions in 21 units (20 need them): 4 owner records of 2026-11-11, 97 of 2026-11-17 under the owner's delegation, 7 of them on the owner's word. 362 survivors stay counted.
- Provenance now binds every tracked file and the platform family; two earlier full campaigns failed to aggregate because of hosting-runner differences and one test that was host dependent, both fixed at their cause.
- Hosted CI green on the head. Release gate closed: single-job DEEP cannot fit its limit, the sharded deep evidence is marked dirty, and no REAL runner is available. Not certified.

Report and owner decisions: `docs/thesis-remediation/MUTATION_CLOSURE_2026-11-17.md`. PR #117 stays a draft; nothing is merged.

Release verification status (PR #117, head `813256b`, CI green).

The full `verify-release` workflow now runs end to end on hosted Linux. Seven wiring defects were found and fixed (merge-commit SHA in the REAL preflights, mutated sources staged in the checkout, bundle size and content limits, PyTorch-importing test collection in the locked REAL environment, gate dependency set, a mutation sandbox file). In the last run (44143370017) FAST, FAULTS, types, tools, reproduction, REAL from public sources and the 45-shard DEEP campaign all pass; the gate rejects the release for one reason, the profiles ran different pandas and pyod versions and differ from the recorded lock.

Decision for the owner: one dependency environment for every profile (recommended: the lock, pandas 3.0.6), which needs a DEEP rerun and revalidation of the 97 delegated equivalence records. Details and the other owner decisions: `docs/thesis-remediation/MUTATION_CLOSURE_2026-11-17.md`, section B. Not certified; the PR stays a draft.
